findings.message: No JSON-LD block in the post.
Hours for sun do not match the ficha.
Internal link points to a page that is not in the ficha page list.
Link could not be confirmed (403); check by hand.

findings.quote: A child's first dental visit should happen at age three.
findings.why: ADA and AAPD recommend the first visit by the first birthday or within six months of the first tooth, not at age three, so this delays care.
findings.fix: Replace with: a child's first dental visit should happen by their first birthday or within six months after the first tooth appears, per ADA and AAPD guidance.

findings.quote: We are open Sundays from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.
findings.why: The ficha lists no Sunday hours (anything not listed is closed), and this also contradicts the correct hours at the end of the post.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence; the correct hours are already given in the final section.

findings.quote: For older siblings, see our [clear aligner page](https://www.bluebonnethollowdental.example/services/clear-aligners).
findings.why: /services/clear-aligners is not among the pages listed in the ficha, so the internal link would be broken.
findings.fix: Remove the link or point to an existing page such as /services.

findings.quote: For a child under two, ask a health professional about fluoride toothpaste; for young children, supervise brushing and encourage spitting rather than swallowing.
findings.why: Mainstream ADA guidance says to use a smear (grain of rice size) of fluoride toothpaste from the first tooth for children under three, so deferring the question for under-twos is inconsistent and the post never states the amount.
findings.fix: State that ADA advises a smear of fluoride toothpaste, about the size of a grain of rice, from the first tooth until age 3, then a pea-sized amount from ages 3 to 6.

findings.quote: Use an age-appropriate amount of fluoride toothpaste based on your dentist’s or doctor’s advice.
findings.why: The vague wording leaves parents without the concrete amounts that ADA guidance provides.
findings.fix: Add the specific ADA amounts (rice-grain smear, then pea-sized).

findings.quote: Water between meals can be a useful choice, while juice and sweet drinks should not be treated as substitutes for water.
findings.why: This is a harmless general statement but is not tied to a specific cited source.
findings.fix: Attribute it to the CDC or AAPD page already listed in Sources if it appears there.

findings.quote: Early dental visits help families talk through brushing, feeding habits, fluoride, and ways to lower the risk of cavities.
findings.why: A general statement that is plausible and consistent with AAPD guidance but is not linked inline to a source.
findings.fix: Add an inline reference to the AAPD source.

findings.quote: Parents often wonder whether a baby will be able to sit still or whether the visit will involve a full cleaning.
findings.why: The generic opener about what parents 'often wonder' reads as filler and is stylistically typical of AI drafts.
findings.fix: Open with a concrete, specific statement about the first visit.
